```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(radiatR)
```

This guide is written for an AI agent asked to analyse directional data with
radiatR, and for the person checking its work. It states the conventions the
package uses, how it fails, and the mistakes that are easy to make. Every code
chunk below is run when the package is built.

## Two ways in

Start from **trajectories** when you have tracking output (x/y positions over
time) and need one heading per track, or from a **table of angles** when the
headings have already been measured.

```{r tracks}
sim <- as.data.frame(simulate_tracks(seed = 1, n_points = 50))
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
write.csv(sim, path, row.names = FALSE)

ts <- read_tracks(
  path,
  mapping   = list(id = "trial_id", time = "frame", x = "abs_x", y = "abs_y"),
  time_type = "frames",
  fps       = 30,
  keep      = "condition"
)
hd <- derive_headings(ts, rule = "distal", carry = "condition")
head(hd, 3)
```

```{r angles}
bearings <- data.frame(bearing = c(10, 20, 350, 5), site = c("a", "a", "b", "b"))
hf <- headings_frame(bearings, col = "bearing", units = "degrees",
                     angle_convention = "clock")
hf
```

## Angle conventions

- Internally every angle is in **radians** in the **unit-circle convention**:
  0 points East and angles increase counter-clockwise. Headings derived from
  tracks lie in [0, 2*pi).
- `headings_frame()` converts on the way in. `units` has no default.
  `angle_convention = "clock"` means 0 = North, increasing clockwise (compass
  bearings); `"unit_circle"` means the data are already 0 = East,
  counter-clockwise. In the example above a bearing of 10 degrees is stored as
  `r round(hf$bearing[1], 3)` radians.
- `headings_frame()` does not wrap values supplied in the unit-circle
  convention: 370 degrees is stored as `r round(370 * pi / 180, 2)` radians and
  -20 degrees as `r round(-20 * pi / 180, 2)`. Wrap them yourself if a later
  step needs [0, 2*pi).
- Summary tables carry two columns. `mean_dir` is in radians, unit-circle
  convention. `mean_dir_deg` is in the **display convention** set by
  `circ_display()`, which by default is 0 = North, clockwise. It is therefore
  not `mean_dir * 180 / pi`.

```{r summary}
circ_summarise(hd, col = "heading", units = "radians", .by = "condition")
```

State the convention whenever you report a direction.

## Coordinates and calibration

Heading rules that use a radius (`crossing`, `exit`, `entry`, `ring_tangent`,
`distal` with `max_radius`) read radii in the units of the coordinates the
`Tracks` object holds. Decide how those coordinates relate to the arena before
choosing a rule.

- `normalize_xy = FALSE` (the default) keeps x/y as supplied.
- `origin = c(x, y)` with `radius` is **calibration**: every trajectory is
  mapped with `(xy - origin) / radius`, so the arena edge is at radius 1 and
  bearings from the arena centre are preserved. Supply both together.
- `normalize_xy = TRUE` rescales each trajectory on its own bounding box. It
  preserves shape only and does **not** preserve bearing from a fixed arena
  centre. It is not calibration and cannot be combined with `origin`/`radius`.

## Map every column yourself

- Without a dialect, `read_tracks()` keeps only the mapped columns and those
  named in `keep` (a dialect keeps the columns it produces). Name every
  grouping column you will need later in `keep`, then bring it onto the
  headings with `derive_headings(carry = )`. A group comparison on a column
  that was not kept fails with "column ... not found".
- A name in `keep` or `carry` that is not in the data is dropped without a
  message. Check the result has the columns you asked for.
- A `carry` name that is already a column of the result (`id`, `time`,
  `heading`) is an error: the carried values would overwrite the derived ones.
- A role missing from `mapping` is guessed from the column names. An unmapped
  column called `theta`, `angle`, `phi`, `bearing`, `deg` or `degrees` becomes
  the angle, read in radians unless `angle_unit` says otherwise; one called
  `w`, `weight` or `weights` becomes the weight. Map `id`, `time`, `x` and `y`
  explicitly, and check `guess_columns()` on the table before loading.

## Time

- `time_type` says how the time column is expressed: `"frames"`, `"seconds"`
  or `"posix"`. Prefer stating it to relying on `"auto"`.
- `time_type = "frames"` requires `fps`. The frame rate is stored on the
  `Tracks` object and used by `elapsed_seconds()` and the kinematics functions.
- radiatR never assumes a frame rate. Supply `fps`, or set it afterwards with
  `set_frame_rate()`.

## Failures are information

radiatR stops rather than guessing. Read the error; do not work around it.

| Condition class | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `radiatR_invalid_rows` | x/y missing or non-finite; the error lists rows and ids |
| `radiatR_malformed_values` | a column holds values that are not numeric; lists rows and values, and `suggested_decimal` when they look written with the other decimal mark |
| `radiatR_ambiguous_decimal` | a `;` file's sniffed decimal point is shown only outside the role columns, which hold values like `1.234` (1.234 or 1234?); pass `read_opts = list(decimal = )` (also raised when no data row of the first 20 lines is whole) |
| `radiatR_invalid_tracks` | the data break a `Tracks` invariant (see `?tracks`) |
| `radiatR_invalid_argument` | an argument cannot be used as given (for `read_opts`: an unknown entry, a bad decimal mark, or an option the dialect cannot use; `option` names it) |
| `radiatR_nonestimable` | a statistic cannot be estimated for a group |
| `radiatR_dropped_rows` | warning raised when `on_invalid = "drop"` removed rows |
| `radiatR_attrition` | message from the `deeplabcut`, `sleap`, `ethovision` and `anymaze` dialects: the points masked at load and the rows left without a position (kept in `@meta$attrition`; not the heading attrition of the next section) |
| `radiatR_dialect_error` | a dialect cannot read the file as that program's output; the message says why |

- `on_invalid = "error"` is the default. `"drop"` removes rows with missing or
  non-finite x/y and warns; it is a decision about the data, so report it.
- When the same id appears in more than one file, the default
  `id_collision = "error"` stops. `"namespace"` prefixes each id with its
  file's name (less extension; the full name or the end of the path where files share that).

## Heading rules and attrition

`derive_headings()` returns one row per track (some rules can return more).
When a rule yields no heading for a track, the row is kept with `NA` and the
result carries `n_total` and `n_missing` (headings, i.e. rows), `n_trials`
(distinct trials) and `missing_ids` (each trial with a missing heading, once)
attributes.
`on_missing` controls what else happens: `"warn"` (the default) raises a
warning, `"error"` stops, `"quiet"` says nothing. The `ransac_straight` rule
draws random numbers, so call `set.seed()` before it.

```{r attrition}
attr(hd, "n_total")
attr(hd, "n_missing")
```

Attrition is often not random: a track that never reaches a ring has no
`crossing` heading, and those animals may differ from the rest. Report
`n_missing` alongside any statistic, and do not switch rules silently to
recover the missing tracks.

## Tests

```{r tests}
set.seed(1)
test_uniformity(hd, group_col = "condition", angle_col = "heading")
test_mean_directions(hd, group_col = "condition", angle_col = "heading")
```

- `test_uniformity()` asks whether headings are uniform around the circle;
  `test = "vtest"` tests against an expected direction `mu`, in radians.
- `test_mean_directions()`, `test_concentration()` and `test_distributions()`
  compare groups.
- Pass `axial = TRUE` for bidirectional data (an axis, not a direction).
- Monte Carlo and permutation p-values, and the bootstrap functions, use R's
  random number generator. Call `set.seed()` first and report the seed.

## Pitfalls

1. Reporting `mean_dir_deg` as if it were counter-clockwise from East.
2. Treating `normalize_xy = TRUE` as calibration.
3. Forgetting `keep` / `carry`, or misspelling a name in them, then finding
   the grouping column is gone.
4. Using `on_invalid = "drop"` without saying how many rows were dropped.
5. Ignoring `n_missing` after `derive_headings()`.
6. Giving radii to a heading rule in the wrong units.
7. Reporting a resampling p-value without a seed.
8. Catching an error and carrying on with a different method.
9. Letting `read_tracks()` guess an angle or weight column from its name.

## Driving radiatR through tools

`radiatR_tools()` returns tool definitions for the
[ellmer](https://ellmer.tidyverse.org) package. They let a model run an
analysis without writing R: load tracks or a table of headings, derive
headings, summarise, test and plot.

Serve them to an MCP client such as Claude Code or Claude Desktop with the
[mcptools](https://posit-dev.github.io/mcptools/) package:

```sh
claude mcp add radiatR -- Rscript -e \
  'mcptools::mcp_server(tools = radiatR::radiatR_tools(), session_tools = FALSE)'
```

Or register them with an ellmer chat:

```{r ellmer-chat, eval = FALSE}
chat <- ellmer::chat_anthropic()
chat$register_tools(radiatR_tools())
```

What the tools guarantee:

- **Handles.** Loaded and derived objects are referred to by name
  (`tracks_1`, `headings_1`). They live in the server process, so they cannot
  be inspected from another R console.
- **Code.** Every result includes the R code that produced it, and
  `radiatR_export_script` returns the whole session as one script. Running
  that script reproduces the data objects and result tables exactly. Save it
  with the analysis.
- **Nothing filled in.** The time type, the unit of a mapped angle column,
  and the unit and convention of a table of angles must be stated. A missing
  argument is an error, never a default, and so is an option the chosen test
  or method would ignore. A column that `read_tracks()` would pick up by name
  as an angle or weight is refused, and so is a name in `keep`, `carry` or a
  grouping argument that is not in the data. A table of angles whose rows
  differ in length is refused. Heading derivation and every test take a seed.
- **Nothing hidden.** Warnings and printed output come back in the result
  under `warnings` and `output`. An error message names the condition
  classes, the call that failed, and anything raised before the failure.
- **Numbers.** Results are given to 15 significant digits; missing and
  non-finite values appear as the strings `"NA"`, `"NaN"`, `"Inf"`, so a
  missing string cannot be told from the text `"NA"`. The script holds the
  exact values.

Limits to know about:

- `radiatR_load_tracks` reads a file as `read_tracks()` does: the delimiter
  and the decimal mark are detected from the file, not stated. A wrong
  detection fails with `radiatR_malformed_values` or
  `radiatR_ambiguous_decimal` rather than loading wrong numbers.
- A mapped angle column must already be in the unit-circle convention;
  `read_tracks()` has no convention argument.
- A file with a column named like an angle or a weight (`theta`, `angle`,
  `phi`, `bearing`, `deg`, `degrees`, `w`, `weight`, `weights`) that is not
  one cannot be loaded through the tools until the column is renamed:
  `read_tracks()` cannot be told to leave it alone.

The tools cover the common path only. To let the agent also read help pages
and vignettes, serve them together with the documentation tools of the
[btw](https://posit-dev.github.io/btw/) package:
`tools = c(btw::btw_tools("docs"), radiatR::radiatR_tools())`.

An MCP server talks over standard output, so anything R prints at startup
breaks the connection. In a project that uses renv, start the server with
`RENV_CONFIG_SYNCHRONIZED_CHECK=FALSE` so renv's status line is not printed.
